title: Full-Stack DS Component Contract
description: Defines the contract for a component: anatomy, props, tokens, a11y, behavior, and usage. Implementation-language-agnostic — any target that can read these fields can reconstruct the component.

$schema.description: Path to this JSON Schema file for editor validation.

schemaVersion.description: Contract schema version. Absent or "1" indicates the current iteration.

codegen.description: Codegen behavior overrides for this contract. All fields optional; unset uses defaults.

tests.description: Whether to emit a test file. Default true. Set false for components with hand-authored tests that codegen should not overwrite.

description.description: Brief human-readable summary of the component's purpose.

layer.description: Architecture layer per the component-complexity blueprint: 'primitive' (irreducible to the user, e.g. Button, Input, Icon), 'compound' (blessed bundle of primitives with ARIA wiring but no state orchestration, e.g. TextField, Card, Chip), 'composer' (orchestrates state, focus, dismissal, or multi-step interaction, e.g. Dialog, Popover, Field, Tabs), or 'assembly' (product flow; assemblies live in the app, not the system).

category.description: Behavioral family axis — documentation, grouping, and token-coverage. NOT a geometry axis: visual box-model defaults are driven by the separate 'morphology' field (docs/contract-group-axes.md). 'action' (button-like: Button, Switch), 'input' (form controls: Input, TextField, Select, Checkbox), 'surface' (containers: Card, Sheet, Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Toast), 'feedback' (status: Alert, Progress, Skeleton, Status), 'glyph' (atomic visual: Icon, Avatar, Badge, ProfileFlag), 'display' (inline content / structural visual: Text, Label, Chip, Image, Links, Stat, Truncate, Divider), 'structure' (collection layout: Table, Tabs, Accordion, NavList, List, Breadcrumbs). Codegen does not consume this field.

morphology.description: OPTIONAL geometry / default-affordance axis (the morphology axis anticipated by docs/contract-group-axes.md). Selects a StyleProfile that supplies box-model slot defaults plus root structural CSS (display / box-sizing / flow), layered BETWEEN the BoxModel primitive defaults and the component token sidecar — the sidecar still wins. When absent, the component keeps the legacy two-way primitive-under-sidecar merge (unchanged behavior). Values: 'fixed-square' (true glyphs sized to a square extent: Icon, Avatar), 'content-inline' (inline labels that size to content with padding + min-height: Badge), 'identity-inline' (avatar + text identity row, content width: ProfileFlag), 'linear-meter' (full-width bar, explicit thickness, zero padding: Progress linear), 'loading-block' (content-shaped loading block that stretches with explicit min-height: Skeleton), 'replaced-media' (native replaced element — display block, max-width 100%, height auto: Image).

cssPrefix.description: BEM block name override. Defaults to kebab-cased component name.

anatomy.description: Named sub-parts that make up the component. Legacy forms (string array or {parts, description}) remain valid; prefer the detailed form which attaches roles and metadata to each part.

oneOf.description: Simple list of anatomy part names (legacy).

parts.description: Ordered canonical list of anatomy part names.

description.description: Prose explaining how the parts relate to each other.

details.description: Per-part metadata keyed by part name. Keys should appear in `parts`.

dom.description: Optional DOM tree describing how parts compose into rendered elements with attribute and event bindings. Framework emitters walk this tree when present; otherwise they fall back to single-root output.

props.description: Component prop API in the six-bucket form. New contracts should use `designed` + `passthrough` and (where applicable) `constrained` / `restricted`. The `styled` and `hook` buckets are accepted as legacy surfaces during migration; both carry the same shape they had under the open-keyed schema.

designed.description: Props the component intentionally exposes as part of its designed API. Every member must have a non-empty description.

passthrough.description: HTML attribute surface the component deliberately forwards to its root element. `extends` names the HTML element whose attribute surface is inherited (e.g. "button", "input", "div"); the emitter uses this to forward attributes without guessing.

extends.description: HTML element whose attribute surface is forwarded, e.g. 'button', 'input', 'div'.

allowed.description: Explicit allowlist of forwarded attribute names. If absent, every attribute of the extended element is forwarded.

constrained.description: Props that are valid only under specific conditions. Each member must describe its constraint.

restricted.description: Props that must NOT be passed by consumers. Each member must describe why.

styled.description: Legacy surface — migrate to `designed` + `passthrough` when updating this contract.

hook.description: Props surfaced via a companion hook (e.g. useDialog). Migrate to `designed` when updating this contract.

channels.description: Controlled/uncontrolled prop pairings. Each channel groups the props that together drive one piece of externally observable state.

types.description: Named type definitions referenced by prop members.

dataModel.description: Shapes of domain objects the component consumes (e.g. option records, tree nodes). Use when props reference array/object types that need structural definition for non-TS implementers.

variants.description: Variant dimensions keyed by prop name, each listing allowed values.

states.description: Interaction/visual states as orthogonal dimensions (axes). Each dimension is a stackable axis whose values are (by default) mutually exclusive; dimensions compose. This is the sole authoring form — the legacy flat string[] branch has been removed.

dimensions.description: Orthogonal state axes keyed by axis name (e.g. pointer/focus/availability/selection). By default each dimension is mutually exclusive (one active value at a time).

keyframes.description: CSS @keyframes definitions. Keys are animation names, values are objects mapping keyframe selectors (from, to, 50%, etc.) to CSS property-value pairs.

events.description: Structured signatures for user-facing callbacks (onChange, onOpen, onClose, etc.). Keys are event names — not prop names — and may be emitted through one or more props listed in `emittedVia`.

dismissal.description: How a dismissable surface can be closed. Accepts either the structured form ({ triggers: [...] }) or a legacy flat array of event names — the flat form lets older portfolio contracts import unchanged.

oneOf.description: Legacy flat form: array of event names. Equivalent to { triggers: [{ event: <name> }, ...] }.

slots.description: Named slot anchors keyed by slot name. Each entry declares whether the slot is required and an optional CSS selector consumers or test harnesses can use to locate the slot in rendered output. Complements anatomy.details — anatomy describes the part's semantic role; slots describes its DOM anchor.

required.description: Two senses, distinguished by part ownership. For consumer-supplied regions (anatomy.dom named slots, public subcomponents): every valid composition must supply the region — curated usage frames are audited against this (FEAT-SLOT-REQUIRED-USAGE-BINDING-01). For component-owned anchors: the anchor is guaranteed present in rendered output. The `root` entry anchors the host itself.

selector.description: CSS selector that identifies the slot anchor in rendered DOM (e.g. "[data-slot=\"trigger\"]").

ssr.description: Server-side rendering and hydration contract. Tells the codegen and consumers whether the component must be wrapped in a client boundary.

hydrateOn.description: When the component hydrates. "interaction" defers until first user interaction (lazy); "load" hydrates on initial page load; "none" is fully server-rendered with no client behavior.

rtl.description: Right-to-left behavior contract. Currently a single field; structured as an object so additional RTL concerns can be added without a breaking change.

flipIcon.description: Whether directional icons (e.g. chevrons, arrows) should be horizontally mirrored under dir="rtl".

relationships.description: Cross-part wiring (ID references) that implementers must maintain so assistive tech works.

fieldAssociation.description: Declares this component a form control that consumes ambient field association (generated control id + aria-describedby) when slotted into a field composer's control region. The provider side is derived from relationships[] whose target part hosts a consumer slot.

a2ui.description: Agent-facing authoring metadata. Keep lean — the runtime deriver pulls props, enum, default, events, form from the existing contract blocks.

domNode.description: Single DOM node in a component's render tree. Framework emitters map this into idiomatic JSX/SFC/template/html output. A node declares EITHER a native `tag` OR a `componentRef` to another design-system component — never both.

tag.description: HTML tag name (e.g. "label", "input"), or the special sentinel "slot" / "children" where consumer-provided content renders. Mutually exclusive with `componentRef`.

componentRef.description: Reference to another design-system component this node renders, in `fsds.<Name>` form (e.g. "fsds.Button", "fsds.Input"). Resolution is by-reference: the emitter imports the referenced component by relative sibling path and emits it as a component-instance element (`<Button .../>`), never an inline expansion. The referenced component's `layer` must be lower-or-equal to this component's in the ladder primitive < compound < composer < assembly. Mutually exclusive with `tag`.

name.description: Named-slot identifier — only meaningful when `tag === "slot"`. Maps to framework idioms: React `slots.<name>`, Vue/Lit `<slot name="<name>">`, Svelte `{@render <name>?.()}`, Angular `<ng-content select="[slot=<name>]">`. When absent, the slot is the default/unnamed slot.

part.description: Optional reference to an `anatomy.parts` entry. The emitter derives a BEM `__part` class from this.

bindings.description: Dynamic *attribute* bindings keyed by attribute name (e.g. `aria-label`, `disabled`, `src`). A value is either a binding-expression string or a closed `{kind: "map", source, values, fallback?}` projection. Maps lower generically through IR and must exhaust an enumerable source-prop domain unless a fallback is declared. Event handlers belong under `events`; inner content under `content`; JS-only DOM properties belong under `properties`.

properties.description: DOM-property-only bindings — for facts that must be set via an imperative JS property assignment on the live element (e.g. `el.indeterminate = true`), never via an HTML attribute or template-attribute binding (`indeterminate` has no HTML attribute form at all; JSX/Vue/Svelte/Angular/Lit template-attribute syntax cannot express it). Values use the same binding-expression mini-language as `bindings`. Distinct from `bindings` because every attribute-binding lowering path (JSX prop, Vue `:attr`, Angular `[attr]`, Lit `?attr=`, Svelte `attr=`) writes an HTML attribute, which is the wrong mechanism for a property-only fact — each framework emitter instead applies this via its ref/lifecycle idiom (e.g. React `useRef`+`useEffect`).

events.description: Event handlers keyed by *unprefixed* event name (`click`, `input`, `change`, `keydown`, ...). Values use the same binding-expression mini-language as `bindings`, PLUS two event-position-only forms. (1) `channel:<name>.onChange(<arg>)` invokes that channel's setter WITH a per-item payload (FEAT-BINDING-CALL-WITH-ARG-01), e.g. `channel:selection.onChange(iter:item.value)` lowers to `() => setSelection(item.value)`. (2) `channel:<name>.onChange:<op>(<operand>, ...)` applies a NAMED update operation from a closed vocabulary that composes the channel's CURRENT value with the event payload / operands (FEAT-CHANNEL-UPDATE-OPERATIONS-01). Two operations exist: `setCharAt(<index>)` — string channel only — sets the character at `<index>` (an iteration local, e.g. `iter:index`) to the LAST character of the native input payload, preserving all other positions (witness: OTP `channel:value.onChange:setCharAt(iter:index)`; whole-paste distribution across fields is out of scope, a field takes only the last char); and `toggleMembership(<member>, <modeGate>)` — array-capable channel (a `T[]` arm, e.g. `string | string[]`) — where `<modeGate>` is a boolean prop that when false REPLACES (single-select) and when true toggles `<member>`'s membership in the selection array (witness: Select `channel:selection.onChange:toggleMembership(iter:item.value, prop:multiple)`; the mode dispatch is contract-authored via the prop, never a component-name literal in an emitter). For BOTH forms every operand is a closed, value-shaped payload only — `iter:item` / `iter:item.<path>` / `iter:index`, `prop:<name>` / `prop:<name>.<path>`, or `literal:<text>` — never another channel, predicate, conditional, or nested call (no arbitrary-expression escape hatch). The bare `channel:<name>.onChange` (no-arg) form is still legal and lowers to the framework's default DOM-event unwrap. Each framework emitter lowers to its idiom: React `onClick={...}`, Vue `@click="..."`, Svelte `on:click={...}`, Angular `(click)="..."`, Lit `@click=${...}`; the update-operation form composes the next value through the canonical channel setter (Angular via a synthesized method, since its template expressions forbid arrows/spread). Distinct from attribute bindings because Angular and Lit reject event-shaped attribute bindings; the call/operation forms are legal ONLY here (they produce a `() => …` handler, not a value).

oneOf.description: Single inner-content binding (one binding expression). Lowers to the framework's content-projection idiom (React `{prop}`, Vue/Angular `{{ prop }}`, Svelte `{prop}`, Lit `${this.prop}`). Mutually exclusive with `children` on the same node — wrap a content value in its own child if you need both.

Content-transform directive: the node's inner content is produced by a named transform applied to a source prop binding, not by projecting the binding verbatim. The transform is an IR-level fact lowered generically by every emitter — no emitter may branch on the host component's name. One transform is admitted today: `highlight` splits the source string into syntax tokens via the shared pure tokenizer and renders one span per token (the `tokenPart` part class plus a `data-token="<kind>"` attribute; token-kind vocabulary is declared by the component's types). Text-only by construction: token spans carry text children, so the source is never interpreted as markup. Targets that do not realize the transform degrade to plain rendering of the source binding.

transform.description: Transform name. Closed set: highlight | markdown.

source.description: Binding expression naming the string prop that carries the literal source text to tokenize (e.g. "prop:code").

language.description: `highlight` only: binding expression naming the string prop that carries the declared tokenization language (e.g. "prop:language").

gate.description: `highlight` only, optional: binding expression naming the boolean prop that enables the transform. When the gate prop is false the node renders the source binding as a single plain text run instead of token spans.

tokenPart.description: `highlight` only: `anatomy.parts` entry realized as one span per token. The part must exist, be `tag: "span"`, and be marked `multiple: true`.

tokens.description: Optional binding to an externally supplied lossless syntax-token array.

lineNumbers.description: Optional binding to the boolean line-number display prop.

linePart.description: Anatomy part for one lossless source line.

gutterPart.description: Anatomy part for a presentational line number.

oneOf.description: Content-transform directive (markdown, FEAT-MARKDOWN-CONTENT-TRANSFORM-01): the node's inner content is the STRUCTURAL parse of the markdown source prop — block elements and inline marks realized from the anatomy parts named in blockParts/markParts. The grammar is closed: every block kind and mark kind must map to a declared anatomy part whose tag matches the kind's DOM contract (heading h1-h6, paragraph p, unorderedList ul, orderedList ol, listItem li, codeBlock pre, blockquote blockquote; marks emphasis em, strong strong, code code, link a — mark parts must be multiple: true). Text is literal by construction: raw HTML in the source never interprets, and link hrefs are protocol-sanitized at parse time. Targets that do not realize the transform degrade to plain rendering of the source binding. No emitter may branch on the host component's name.

transform.description: Transform name. Closed set: highlight | markdown.

source.description: Binding expression naming the string prop that carries the markdown source (e.g. "prop:content").

gate.description: Optional: binding expression naming the boolean prop that enables the transform. When falsy the node renders the source binding as a single plain text run.

blockParts.description: Block vocabulary: every closed kind maps to an anatomy.parts entry. Total by construction — unmapped kinds cannot silently drop content.

heading.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for heading blocks.

paragraph.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for paragraph blocks.

unorderedList.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for unorderedList blocks.

orderedList.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for orderedList blocks.

listItem.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for listItem blocks.

codeBlock.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for codeBlock blocks.

blockquote.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for blockquote blocks.

markParts.description: Inline-mark vocabulary: every closed kind maps to an anatomy.parts entry (tag span-family per the DOM contract, multiple: true). Text marks render as bare text.

emphasis.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for emphasis marks.

strong.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for strong marks.

code.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for code marks.

link.description: anatomy.parts entry realized for link marks.

content.description: Inner content: either a single binding expression (string form) or a content-transform directive (object form). Mutually exclusive with `children` on the same node — wrap a content value in its own child if you need both.

children.description: Child nodes. Empty/absent for leaf elements. Mutually exclusive with `content` on the same node.

if.description: Render guard. "<prop>" renders when prop is truthy; "!<prop>" renders when prop is FALSY; "children" renders when consumer-provided children exist; "slot:<name>" renders when the consumer fills that named slot, which must sit inside the guarded subtree.

iterate.description: Renders this node N times, driven by a prop. Note: index-keyed iteration only — not suitable for sortable/reorderable lists.

source.description: Iteration source as a binding expression. Either 'prop:X' referencing a contract prop, or 'channel:X.value' referencing a declared channel's resolved value. 'prop:length' for count-driven; 'prop:items' or 'channel:selection.value' for array-driven.

kind.description: 'count' renders N copies (source prop must be number-typed). 'array' renders one copy per item (source prop must be array-typed).

indexVar.description: Local variable name carrying the zero-based loop index. Available to nested binding/content/attr expressions through render-context interpolation.

itemVar.description: Local variable name carrying the current item (only meaningful when kind='array').

itemType.description: TypeScript type of each item, referencing a `types` entry or a builtin. Required when kind='array'.

^--fsds-[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$.description: Binding expression or finite value map, with the same source/domain validation as attribute bindings.

cssVariableBindings.description: CSS custom-property bindings on this element's runtime `style` attribute. Keys must match --fsds-<component>-<name>. Lowers to: React/Vue/Lit object-style; Svelte `style:--x={v}` directive; Angular `[style.--x]` binding. Mutually exclusive with a literal `style` attr on the same node.

iconGlyph.description: Renders this `svg` node's viewBox and `<path>` children from the design-system icon catalog (`@full-stack-ds/iconography`), looked up at runtime by the bound name prop. The emitter stamps `data-fsds-icon="<resolved name>"` on the svg and renders one `<path>` per glyph path record. Only valid on a `tag: "svg"` node; mutually exclusive with `children`, `content`, and `iterate`. When the lookup misses (unknown name), the svg is not rendered. Icon-name reference integrity for literal usages is enforced by generate:check against the built catalog.

nameFrom.description: Binding naming the string-typed prop that carries the canonical icon name (e.g. "prop:name").

sizeFrom.description: Binding naming the prop that carries the requested size. When `sizeHints` is present the prop's value is mapped through it to pixels; otherwise the value is used as a pixel number directly. Drives both authored-variant selection (resolveIcon) and the rendered svg width/height.

sizeHints.description: Map from the size prop's enum values to pixel sizes (e.g. {"sm": 16, "md": 20, "lg": 24, "xl": 32}). Pixel values select the nearest authored glyph variant; they intentionally mirror the icon.size token scale — selection hints are contract semantics, rendered size still tracks these literal pixels.

propMember.description: A single prop exposed by the component. Declares its type as EITHER a legacy TS-string `type` OR a structured framework-neutral `propType` (exactly one) — the same XOR as designedPropMember/constrainedPropMember, so legacy-bucket (styled/hook) members can migrate to the structured grammar in place (CODEGEN-PROP-TYPE-IR-LEGACY-BUCKET-REFS-01).

name.description: Prop name as it appears in the component API.

required.description: Whether the prop must be supplied by the consumer.

default.description: Default value when the prop is omitted. Arrays of primitives are accepted for collection-typed props (e.g. `string[]`); the codegen emits them as JSON literals in the destructure (`= ["a", "b"]`). Object items inside arrays are accepted for typed-object collections (e.g. `WalkthroughStepSpec[]`), as long as every object field is primitive-shaped — the codegen JSON-stringifies the whole literal, so any JSON-serializable shape works mechanically.

nodeKind.description: A2UI disambiguation hint for props whose TS type can't distinguish a nested component from a registered icon (`ReactNode`, `ReactElement`). When present, the A2UI deriver uses this as the prop's `accepts` value instead of guessing. Leave unset for non-node props.

propType.description: Framework-neutral structured prop type (PropTypeIR). V1 (CODEGEN-PROP-TYPE-IR-PILOT-01): string/number/boolean/enum/node/ref. V2 (CODEGEN-PROP-TYPE-IR-OBSERVED-TYPES-01, observed-corpus extension): callback/array/union/literal/void/promise. When present it supersedes the legacy TS-string `type` as the agnostic source the IR normalizes and emitters lower. There is deliberately NO inline anonymous-object kind: named object-ish types use {kind:ref} to a contract alias; a genuinely anonymous object type stays a declared residual (legacy `type`). See docs/a2ui-projection.md.

designedPropMember.description: A prop in the `designed` or `restricted` bucket. `description` is required to be non-empty. Each member declares its type as EITHER a legacy TS-string `type` OR a structured framework-neutral `propType` (exactly one).

description.description: Non-empty description of what this prop controls.

constrainedPropMember.description: A prop in the `constrained` bucket. Adds a required `constraint` field documenting the condition under which the prop is valid. Type is declared as EITHER a legacy TS-string `type` OR a structured `propType` (exactly one).

constraint.description: Human-readable condition under which this prop is valid (e.g. 'only when asChild=true').

propGroup.description: A named group of related props (e.g. styled component props, hook options).

description.description: What this group of props is for.

controlledChannel.description: Declares a controlled/uncontrolled pairing. References existing prop names inside `props.*.members`; does not redefine them.

description.description: What external state this channel represents (e.g. "selected value", "open state", "search query").

value.description: Name of the controlled value prop.

defaultValue.description: Name of the uncontrolled default-value prop, if one exists.

onChange.description: Name of the change handler prop.

enabledBy.description: Name of a sibling prop that must be truthy for this channel to be active (e.g. a search channel enabled by `isSearchable`).

valueType.description: Short type hint for the channel's value (e.g. "number", "string | string[]"). Use when the prop's TS type alone is not descriptive cross-language.

callbackKind.description: Shape of the change-handler callback. "value" (default) means the handler receives the channel's value as its first argument (e.g. (checked: boolean) => void). "event" means the handler receives a framework-native event object the consumer is expected to inspect (e.g. (e: ChangeEvent) => void). Declared explicitly so the IR does not have to infer this from React/DOM type-name heuristics.

notes.description: Free-form notes about semantics (e.g. "in multi mode the value is an array").

omitWhen.description: Condition under which this channel's value is omitted from form submission. Mirrors `form.serialization.omitWhen`. Documents the case rather than implementing it; the codegen reads this to comment the emitted serialization logic.

typeDef.description: A named type used by one or more props.

kind.description: What flavor of type this is.

values.description: Allowed values (required for union and enum kinds).

alias.description: The type expression this aliases (required for alias kind).

dataModel.description: Domain entity shapes consumed by the component. Entity fields use simple type expressions; suffix `?` marks optional.

entities.description: Named entities keyed by entity name.

semantics.description: Prose notes about semantic behaviors over the data model (selection, filtering, ordering, identity).

fields.description: Field name → type expression. Append "?" to the name for optional fields (e.g. "disabled?").

styleBlock.description: CSS property-value pairs for a single selector.

partDetails.description: Metadata about a single anatomy part: what role it plays, whether it's focusable, whether it renders many times, etc.

tag.description: Native HTML tag this part is realized as. When set, the codegen uses this tag for the part's compound subcomponent (skipping Stack wrapping for tags in the table composition set) and for the root component's anatomy.dom node (when the part appears in that tree). If anatomy.dom also declares a tag for the same part, the two must agree. Mutually exclusive with `componentRef`.

componentRef.description: Reference to another design-system component this part is realized as, in `fsds.<Name>` form (e.g. "fsds.Input"). When set, the part is lowered by-reference: the emitter imports the referenced component and emits a component-instance element rather than a native `tag`. The referenced component's `layer` must be lower-or-equal to this component's. Mutually exclusive with `tag`.

subcomponent.description: When true, this part is a consumer-composed compound subcomponent rather than a node owned by the root anatomy.dom tree. The IR emits a separately consumable wrapper carrying this part's class; semantic validation rejects dual ownership by anatomy.dom.

role.description: Conceptual role this part plays in the component's interaction model.

multiple.description: True if this part is rendered many times (e.g. Tabs.tab, Dropdown.option).

focusable.description: Whether this part receives DOM focus. "roving" means it participates in a roving-tabindex group.

interactive.description: Whether this part handles user events directly (click, key, hover).

portalTarget.description: Whether this part renders into a portal rather than inline.

aria.description: Static ARIA contract for this part.

attributes.description: ARIA attributes the implementation must set on this part (e.g. "aria-expanded", "aria-selected").

collapsibleTo.description: Declares that this part's purpose is fully served by a target's native primitive on platforms that ship one. Emitters consult a per-target intent-to-primitive table: targets with a mapping collapse the part into the native primitive; targets without one render the full multi-part anatomy. Web emitters ignore this field. The vocabulary is closed — add new intents in lockstep with the emitters that consume them.

category.description: Semantic domain of this state axis. Component-intrinsic only; app/session/system states stay external to the contract. Cardinality is derived from values.length (2 = boolean, 3+ = enum) — it is not authored.

values.description: Allowed values on this dimension. The `initial` value is the base/absence value and is excluded from the derived flat selector projection.

initial.description: Default (base/absence) value when the component first renders. Excluded from the derived flat selector list (so dimension defaults like rest/enabled/unchecked never emit selectors).

exclusive.description: Whether values on this dimension are mutually exclusive (intra-dimension). Defaults to true. Inter-dimension stackability is structural — dimensions always compose.

suppresses.description: Cross-dimension suppression: when this dimension holds a non-initial value it masks the affordances of the referenced dimensions (e.g. availability=disabled masks interaction). Lowering is realization-aware per target (native :disabled vs aria-disabled).

categories.description: Suppress dimensions whose category is listed here (the common case: availability suppresses interaction).

names.description: Suppress specific dimensions by axis name (escape hatch; prefer categories).

a11y.description: ARIA projection for this dimension. Authored because semantic values (e.g. aria-checked=mixed) must not be fabricated by emitters.

attribute.description: ARIA attribute this dimension drives (e.g. aria-checked, aria-disabled).

derivesFrom.description: Optional value-level derivation override, keyed by dimension value. Each entry pins how that value lowers to a selector/attribute/channel/prop. Omit to use name-based derivation via the shared state→selector mapping.

effect.description: Neutral state-surface effect for the whole dimension. restyle = changes the component's visual treatment (needs a variant axis or styled state layer); overlay = an additive toggled layer representable as a boolean without changing the base style recipe; metadata = retained for documentation/tooling, not a control; channel = runtime/channel-driven, not a user-facing control. valueEffects overrides per value.

valueEffects.description: Value-level effect override, keyed by dimension value. Overrides the dimension-level effect for that value (e.g. openness: open=overlay while opening/closing=channel).

formControlContract.description: Declares the interactive control capability independently from native form serialization. The target part, value channel, value model, and commit semantic are lowered once into IR and shared by framework emitters.

part.description: Rendered anatomy part that owns focus, the value interaction, and any ambient Field association.

channel.description: Controlled/uncontrolled channel updated by this control.

valueModel.description: Semantic shape of the value admitted by this capability. Composite selection controls require a separate capability.

commit.description: When a user interaction commits the channel: per-edit input, platform change, or an activation toggle. Codegen maps this fact to each target's event idiom.

compositeControlContract.description: Declares a repeated-item control whose channel update consumes an enclosing iteration item or index. The capability owns the event; anatomy.dom owns only structure.

part.description: Repeated rendered anatomy part that owns the item interaction.

channel.description: Controlled/uncontrolled channel updated by item interaction.

interactionModel.description: Whether repeated instances select collection values or edit positions in one text value.

commit.description: When the repeated item commits its channel update.

update.description: Closed channelCall or channelUpdate BindingExpression carrying the iteration payload.

formContract.description: Declares how this component participates in HTML forms. Omit for non-form components; set `participates: false` to explicitly record that a component with form-like props does not serialize.

participates.description: Whether this component contributes to a native <form>'s FormData on submit.

inputType.description: Platform input type that backs this control.

name.description: Prop driving the `name` attribute used as the FormData key.

formProp.description: Prop that overrides the owning <form> id.

prop.description: Prop that marks the field as required.

constraintValidation.description: True if the component participates in HTML5 native validation.

valueSource.description: Where the form value originates. Use "channel:<name>" to reference a controlled/uncontrolled pair; "prop:<name>" for a single prop; "static:<literal>" for a fixed value.

omitWhen.description: Condition under which the control contributes no entry to FormData.

multiple.description: True for controls that contribute multiple entries (multi-select, multi-file).

model.description: "native": uses platform validationMessage/setCustomValidity. "props": validity driven purely by props. "hybrid": both, with props taking precedence when set.

invalidProp.description: Prop that forces an invalid visual/AT state.

errorMessageProp.description: Prop that carries the error text shown to users and AT.

errorSurface.description: How the error text is exposed to assistive tech.

ariaAttributes.description: ARIA attributes the implementation must set on the focusable part to reflect validity.

motionContract.description: Motion/animation contract. Durations and easings are authored as token references so they resolve through the cascade and honor brand overrides.

transitions.description: Named animated transitions this component performs.

reducedMotion.description: "respect": honor `prefers-reduced-motion`. "disable": always skip. "reduce": shorter variants. "ignore": do not adapt (strongly discouraged).

reducedMotionStrategy.description: How the reduced-motion adaptation is applied. Free-form.

loops.description: Part-bound repeating motion. Shared web CSS lowering supports opacity and rotation; other targets remain unrealized.

trigger.description: Event or state transition that starts this animation.

phase.description: Semantic phase — useful for reduced-motion heuristics.

focusContract.description: How focus is managed inside and around the component.

strategy.description: "trap": contain focus inside (dialogs). "roving": tabindex moves through siblings. "auto": component sets initial focus on mount/open. "manual": caller controls. "none": no managed focus.

initialFocus.description: Anatomy part name or prop name (prefix prop names with "prop:") that receives focus when first established.

returnFocus.description: Where focus returns when the component closes/unmounts.

wrap.description: For roving focus, whether arrow navigation wraps at the ends.

scrollLock.description: Whether body scroll is locked while focus is managed here (modals).

portalContract.description: Whether and how the component escapes its parent DOM container.

textOverflowContract.description: Target-neutral text-overflow intent. Distinct from any DOM-realization mechanism (e.g. CSS line-clamp custom-property bindings authored on anatomy.dom nodes) — this block declares the semantic fact; DOM targets additionally lower it through the existing cssVariableBindings mechanism (both coexist).

kind.description: The overflow-intent family. Only "line-clamp" (multi-line clamp to a line count) is modeled today; single-line ellipsis, fade, scroll, and expandable overflow are distinct kinds reserved for future extension, not folded into this one.

line.description: The prop supplying the line count, as "prop:<name>". Must be the SAME prop that any existing cssVariableBindings line-clamp realization already reads — this is a second declaration of an existing source, not a new authority over the value.

dismissalContract.description: How a dismissable component can be closed.

targetPart.description: Anatomy part that owns this trigger's interaction (required for overlayClick): the dismissal click handler binds on this element, not the root — the root is pointer-events:none under a full-cover overlay and can never be the hit target (FIX-OVERLAY-CLICK-DISMISSAL-BINDING-01).

surfaceContract.description: Declares this component as a presence surface (see docs/presence-surfaces.md). Coordinates anatomy part roles with presence, modality, anchoring, positioning, and controller selection. Does NOT duplicate the existing portal, dismissal, or focus blocks — those remain the detailed policy knobs; surface is the semantic and controller-selection descriptor.

kind.description: Semantic presence-surface family. Selects the controller family (e.g. AnchoredSurfaceController for tooltip/popover/menu/select; DialogSurfaceController for dialog; ToastSurfaceController for toast).

presence.description: Lifecycle expectation. Ephemeral surfaces close when their trigger condition expires or a timing budget elapses. Persistent surfaces remain until explicitly dismissed.

modality.description: Whether the surface blocks interaction with content outside itself. Blocking surfaces require focus trap, outside inertness, and overlay scrim (specifics live in the top-level focus and portal blocks).

modalityProp.description: Boolean prop that makes a blocking surface non-blocking when false. Requires modality "blocking". When the prop is false the focus trap and scroll lock stay inactive; the contract binds aria-modal and the backdrop's visibility to the same prop.

anchor.description: Relationship to the element the surface is positioned against. Omit for unanchored surfaces (centered modal dialogs, viewport-edge toasts). Two source forms: a trigger anatomy part (popover/tooltip — the invoking element lives in the component's own tree), or a runtime CSS selector carried in a prop (coachmark/guided tour — the anchor is an arbitrary page element outside the component).

part.description: Anatomy part name that registers the invoking element. Must reference a part whose details.role === 'trigger'.

relation.description: Semantic ARIA relation between the trigger element and the surface content.

prop.description: Name of an array-typed prop whose elements carry the anchor selectors (e.g. 'steps').

path.description: Member of each array element that holds the CSS selector string (e.g. 'anchor').

indexChannel.description: Channel whose numeric value selects the active array element (e.g. 'step'). Selector-anchored surfaces open programmatically, so surface.openTriggers stays optional.

part.description: Anatomy part name that registers the rendered surface element. Expected to reference a part whose details.role is one of 'content', 'region', or 'overlay' depending on kind.

interactive.description: Whether the content accepts direct user interaction (focusable controls, links). False for tooltips and toasts.

positioning.description: Placement strategy family. Detailed portal target/layering lives in the top-level portal block.

strategy.description: anchored: relative to the trigger element. centered: viewport-centered. viewport-edge: pinned to a viewport edge (toasts, side sheets). fullscreen: occupies the entire viewport (full-screen takeover; vocabulary reserved — no corpus contract uses it yet). inline: rendered in document flow (no portal).

placementProp.description: Name of the consumer-facing prop that controls preferred placement (e.g. 'placement', 'side').

collision.description: Edge-avoidance behavior when anchored placement would overflow the viewport.

dismissal.description: Semantic dismissal modes expected for this surface. The existing top-level dismissal block carries prop-level enablement (e.g. closeOnEscape: boolean enabledBy). The two compose; they do not replace each other.

openTriggers.description: Interactions on the anchor element that open the surface. Required by IR validation when surface.kind === 'tooltip' or surface.positioning.strategy === 'anchored'; otherwise optional (e.g. toasts and centered dialogs do not have an anchor-driven open trigger).

timing.description: Names of the consumer-facing props that control surface timing. Default values live in the props.styled.members[].default field, as today.

openDelayProp.description: Prop name controlling delayed open (ms before opening once trigger condition starts).

closeDelayProp.description: Prop name controlling delayed close (ms before closing once trigger condition ends).

autoDismissProp.description: Prop name controlling timed auto-dismiss (ms after which the surface closes regardless of trigger). Used by ephemeral surfaces like Toast.

eventSignature.description: Describes the payload of a callback.

stateMachine.description: Declarative state-transition model. References dimension values from `states.dimensions` using "<dimension>=<value>" syntax.

event.description: Trigger name. Semantic validation requires it to resolve to a declared referent: a channels key, an events key, a prop name, a dismissal.triggers[].event, an a11y.keyboard[].id, a "<part>.<verb>" form whose part is declared in anatomy.parts, or a member of the closed DOM platform set (animationend, transitionend). FEAT-STATEMACHINE-TRIGGER-BINDING-01.

from.description: Source state(s). Accepts a single state name or an array of names for shared-target transitions (e.g. both 'hover' and 'focus' transitioning to 'visible' without duplicating entries).

relationship.description: An ID-reference link between two anatomy parts, expressed so implementers know which ARIA attributes to wire.

keyboardEntry.description: A keyboard interaction. Three forms accepted: (1) bare string (legacy); (2) structured ours: { key, action, when?, mode? }; (3) structured portfolio: { key, when, then } — portfolio contracts import unchanged. `then` is an alias for `action`; downstream consumers should treat them equivalently.

action.description: What happens when the key is pressed.

when.description: Anatomy part that must hold focus for this binding to apply.

mode.description: State condition required for this binding (e.g. "openness=expanded").

id.description: Stable interaction identifier for this binding (e.g. "arrow.next" shared by ArrowRight and ArrowDown). stateMachine transition events may resolve to this id when the semantic trigger spans several physical keys (FEAT-STATEMACHINE-TRIGGER-BINDING-01).

behavior.description: Closed realization vocabulary (FEAT-A11Y-COMPOSITE-KEYBOARD-01). When present, the Semantic IR lowers the entry into an emitted keydown realization on the `when` part's node in every web framework; the op sequence derives only from declared facts. `open` requires exactly one boolean channel (set true, then move focus into the surface per `focus.initialFocus`, or to the first item when already open). `select` requires `compositeControl.part === when` (activate the item through the composite channel exactly as its pointer activation does, then, when the contract declares dismissal and `focus.returnFocus`, close and refocus the return part). `roving-*` requires `focus.strategy === "roving"` and a declared roving item set — a `compositeControl` item part or an anatomy part carrying `focusable: "roving"` (move DOM focus among the item parts, honoring `focus.orientation` and `focus.wrap`). Absent `behavior`, the entry is declaration-only: realized by native host semantics (button Enter/Space) or a behavior primitive (dismissal Escape), which the a11y-realization audit classifies.

oneOf.description: Portfolio-shape keyboard entry. `then` is the action; treat as an alias for `action` in the structured-ours form.

id.description: Stable interaction identifier, as in the structured-ours form; stateMachine transition events may resolve to it.

roles.description: All ARIA roles when multiple are used. Use alongside `role` when the component takes more than one role across its anatomy.

apgPattern.description: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide pattern name (e.g. "accordion", "dialog", "combobox"). Helps agent tooling and a11y review route to the correct interaction expectations. Nullable to make explicit absence distinguishable from forgotten field.

obligations.description: Typed acknowledgements of unresolved ARIA obligations the contract cannot yet satisfy (A11Y-CONTRACT-OBLIGATION-VALIDATOR-01). When the static-role validator finds a missing required attribute, an entry here downgrades the failure to an advisory diagnostic. Every suppression records the upstream blocker that would let the contract declare the real obligation.

role.description: ARIA role the suppression applies to, matching the role found in `anatomy.dom`.

attr.description: Required attribute the contract cannot yet provide (e.g. "aria-selected").

reason.description: Why the obligation can't be met today, and the slice/issue that would unblock the real fix.

a2uiContract.description: Slim, agent-facing authoring block. Only fields that can't be derived from other contract blocks live here.

category.description: Broad agent-facing grouping. `content` for static or semi-static text/media containers (Blockquote, Postcard); `layout` for arrangement primitives (Field, List).

usageHints.description: Short imperative notes that improve agent selection and prop-filling.

children.description: Whether and how this component accepts child nodes in the A2UI adjacency list.
